best_hook.why: 'Lady Juliana Ashcroft, you are accused of witchcraft, unlawful healing, and poisoning' - a self-explaining, high-stakes opener.

best_cliffhanger.why: The judge rises and raises his hand to pronounce sentence on the defiant heroine - cut before the verdict.

must_promos.why: 'Renounce these practices to save yourself' - 'No' - 'refusal may be proof of witchcraft' - 'Then let it be', gavel, and the sentence left hanging.
Witchcraft charge read out, heroine admits to healing, then her own maid, begged to 'tell the truth', sobs 'Yes' against her - betrayal lands, we hold on Juliana's hurt.

standalone_risk: A stranger can't see that the maid was coerced or why the lord is prosecuting; that a witchcraft verdict means death is implied, not stated.
notes: Courtroom Q&A is repetitive in the middle (townsman, old woman); the opening charge and the final refusal-to-sentence run are the ad beats.
